pr_title: Follow real AtlanticPassAPCZoneControlZone physical mode on Overkiz (HEAT, COOL or HEAT_COOL)

## Proposed change
<!--

  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.

The following PR: #110510 introduced simple support for ZoneControlZone for Atlantic devices.

Temperature change when AUTO mode is enable, was changing cooling as well as heating temperature, this could be lead to unexpected switch between heating/cooling, as well as higher power consumptions.

This PR fixes that and simplifies the logic by always using a single mode for the subsidiary Zones (the mode depends of the physical configuration of the zone, one of  HEAT_COOL, HEAT or COOL).

![Screenshot](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/211541/5ac93c92-be26-4e1c-a9ff-074e157333c9)

With this fix, hvac_action is set correctly, reflecting the real heating / cooling operating state.
Now, min/max temperature are also in synced with the device configuration.

Like the introduction of the support for those device is included in the 2024.03 release, it would be great to also introduce this fix/refactor. (It's better for the users waiting for the support of those device, since it would not provoke a change of interface in future release)

@iMicknl @MartinHjelmare I would like some feedback on those changes.

I simplified the logic by considering Zones having only one mode (depending on the zone device capabilities) in addition to `OFF`. The mode can be `HEAT`, `COOL` or `HEAT_COOL` and does not change through the life of the device.

It should prevent some unexpected behavio when switching the main device between AUTO, COOLING or HEATING.

I still preserve the `is_using_derogated_temperature_fallback` for backward compatibility purpose, even if I don't have yet the knowledge of a device with this Widget / ControllableName, falling into this consideration.
Why did you change the target branch to rc?

This PR introduces some fixes for the #110510 that has been added to the release, as well as a better way of handling those newly supported devices.

I think it would be great to have it on this release, so that the users waiting for this implementations will directly have this way of controlling the device and it will not change in a future release (cf. #89746 and #108211 )

However I was not sure about the process here, so if you think it's too much changes and it should be postpone until next month, I can switch it back to dev.

That's not the issue, the issue is that there is two temperatures in HASS and the device: cooling and heating.

It's really not easy to explain in simple words but I'lol try.

The device have a lot of temperatures but let's say we are in manual mode to simplify. There is:
* targetHeatingTemperature (get, set)
* targetCoolingTemperature (get, set)
* targetTemperature (get, refresh)

We have then two scenario:

* we turn the thermostat up to 20º, only targetTemperature will get updated and only if the refresh method has been called
* we turn the thermostat to 20/24 in HomeAssistant with my new system, check PR screenshots (meaning 20 heating, 24 cooling). I update respectfully targetHeatingTemperature and targetCoolingTemperature.

targetTemperature get also updated using heating/cooling temperature, I'm not sure about the trigger there.

Knowing that, when the thermostat update the temperature, I'm not advertise directly, I need to manually call the refresh method (for example every 30seconds), doable but need more work.
But once I get this value it's not safe to erase either one of the heating/cooling on HASS because it's not really the truth.

I'm still trying to find a reliable way to do it knowing those devices pretty limited API (or limitations at least).
